an4.244:1.11: For it’s certainly the king’s men who tie his arms tightly behind his back with a strong rope, shave his head, march him from street to street and square to square to the beating of a harsh drum, take him out the south gate, and there, to the south of the city, chop off his head.
an4.244:2.5: For it’s certainly this man who put on a black cloth, messed up his hair, put a club on his shoulder, approached the large crowd, and says:
an4.244:2.6: “Sirs, I’ve done a bad and reprehensible deed, deserving of clubbing. I do whatever makes my fellow monks happy.”
an4.244:3.6: For it’s certainly this man who put on a black cloth, messed up his hair, put a sack of ashes on his shoulder, approached the large crowd, and says:
an4.244:3.7: “Sirs, I’ve done a bad and reprehensible deed, deserving of a sack of ashes;
an4.244:3.8: I do whatever makes my fellow monks happy.”
an4.244:4.6: For it’s certainly this man who put on a black cloth, messed up his hair, approached the large crowd, and says:
an4.244:4.7: “Sirs, I’ve done a bad and reprehensible deed, deserving of criticism;
an4.244:4.8: I do whatever makes my fellow monks happy.”
